title: Longest Common Prefix
problemStatement: Find the longest common prefix of an array of strings.
intuition: The answer can never be longer than the shortest string, and the first mismatching column ends it. Scanning column by column lets you stop at the earliest possible moment.

approaches.title: Vertical scan
approaches.idea: Compare character i across all strings; stop at the first disagreement.
approaches.dryRun:
["flower","flow","flight"]
i=0 all f; i=1 all l; i=2 o vs o vs i -> stop -> "fl"
approaches.whyWorks: A common prefix of length k requires agreement in every column below k.

approaches.title: Sort-based trick
approaches.idea: After sorting, only the first and last strings need comparing.
approaches.whyWorks: Lexicographic extremes bound the common prefix of everything in between.

edgeCases: An empty string in the list -> ""
commonMistakes: Indexing past the end of a shorter string
Returning the whole first string when it is itself the prefix but shorter matches exist
patternRecognition: Prefix problems -> vertical scan or a trie for repeated queries
followUps: Use a trie when queries repeat (#440)
Longest common prefix of two strings only
interviewInsight: The sorted trick is a nice flourish, but explain why it works — otherwise it looks like a memorised hack.
